title: Malaya
capsule: This entry refers to the Malay kingdom (Melayu/Malayu) in Sumatra as it existed in the late 13th–mid 14th century, centered on the Batanghari River system in present-day Jambi province. After the earlier Srivijayan hegemony dissolved, the Dharmasraya polity — successor to Melayu — controlled trade routes in the region; around 1275 a Javanese Singhasari expedition under Kertanagara established overlordship. By the early 14th century the polity had shifted its center northward to Pagarruyung as a Majapahit vassal, with the ruling family Islamizing in the late 14th century. The precise political structure and territorial limits of this transitional Malay polity between c. 1294 and 1352 remain sparsely documented.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. This polity is poorly attested; sources consist largely of Javanese court poetry (Nagarakretagama), Chinese tributary records, and limited archaeological finds from the Batanghari valley — territorial extent is speculative.
